title: OEM Parts Price Bulletin
text: OEM replacement parts prices rose +9.2% during 2024 and a further +4.6% in 2025, a cumulative increase of roughly 14%. Parts cost remains the primary driver of auto physical damage severity nationwide, with every region reporting higher average repair bills.

title: Actuarial Trend Selection Memo â€” Q1
text: Medical care CPI has risen approximately 18% cumulatively since 2023Q1 and continues to outpace general inflation. We assess medical inflation as the dominant driver of bodily injury severity countrywide and recommend maintaining elevated BI severity trend selections.

title: Legal Operations Quarterly Review
text: Attorney representation rates on Northeast BI claims climbed from 48% to 57% over the review period. Represented claims settle approximately 25% higher than unrepresented ones. Litigation climate is now the primary driver of BI severity in the Northeast, amplifying the effect of medical inflation.

title: Catastrophe Event Report â€” 2024Q3 Hurricane
text: A hurricane made landfall in the South region late in 2024Q3. Auto claim counts spiked +18% in 2024Q3 and +10% in 2024Q4 before normalizing. The event is overwhelmingly the driver of the South frequency spike in late 2024.

title: Repair Network Cost Study
text: Vehicles equipped with ADAS sensor suites cost approximately 22% more to repair than non-ADAS equivalents, and ADAS vehicles rose from 45% to 61% of the repairable fleet â€” a significant contributor to PD severity nationally. Separately, parts delivery delays peaked at 9.1 days in 2024Q2 and remain at 6.3 days; supplement handling adds about $180 per claim, a modest contributor to severity.

title: Mobility & Exposure Digest
text: Vehicle-miles traveled grew +2.1% year over year. Higher mileage is a mild upward pressure on accident frequency nationwide, though it explains little of any single region's movement.

title: Winter Operations Flash â€” Polar Vortex
text: The January polar vortex lifted Midwest auto frequency by about +6% for 2025Q1 only. We assess this as a minor, one-quarter effect with no lasting impact on trend.

title: Collision Parts Vendor Newsletter
text: Aftermarket parts availability has improved but not normalized; supplement volumes remain elevated, adding roughly $180 per claim. Supply-chain friction remains a modest contributor to PD severity.

title: Quarterly Severity Attribution — Q4
text: Average repair ticket grew +6.1% in Q4. OEM parts prices remain the primary contributor, with dealer labor rates a major secondary factor at +7.8%. Rental duration lengthened again — a significant, persistent cost.

title: Rental & Towing Cost Review
text: Rental reimbursement rates rose +11% in 2024 as rental fleets shrank, a moderate contributor to severity. Rental duration on repair claims grew from 9.1 to 12.4 days.

title: Repair Labor Rate Survey
text: Dealer labor rates rose +7.8% in 2024Q4 alone — a major driver of auto-pd severity. Labor now accounts for 41% of the average collision repair ticket.

title: Valuation Trends Memo
text: Used-car values fell -12% through 2025, a mild factor: total-loss severity eased while frequency on financed vehicles edged up.

title: Catastrophe Event Report — 2025Q3 Hail
text: The 2025Q3 hail season hit the Southwest corridor twice, lifting auto-pd frequency about +9% for one quarter — significant but episodic.

title: Medical Bill Review Quarterly
text: Telehealth-based PT billing grew 4x since 2024, a moderate contributor to BI severity. 18% of billed sessions lack a supporting clinical note.

title: Legal Media Monitor
text: Attorney advertising spend on BI claims rose +26% year over year; Northeast represented-claim share reached 61%. Litigation climate remains a significant regional driver.

title: Actuarial Trend Selection Memo — Q2
text: Medical care CPI continues to outpace general inflation; medical inflation remains the dominant driver of BI severity countrywide. Litigation climate is major in the Northeast.

title: Supply Chain & Cycle Time Review
text: Parts delivery delays peaked at 9.1 days in 2024Q2 and remain at 6.3 days. Supplement handling adds roughly $180 per claim — a significant, persistent contributor to auto-pd severity.

title: Market Bulletin — OEM Parts Pricing
text: Tier-one suppliers announced another quarterly increase: OEM parts prices remain the primary contributor to repair severity, with the average parts ticket up +6.1% year over year as of Q4. Analysts expect the pass-through to persist into 2026.

title: Market Watch — Northeast BI Litigation
text: Represented-claim share in the Northeast reached 61%, and attorney advertising spend keeps rising. Litigation remains a significant regional driver of bodily-injury severity — insurers should price the corridor accordingly.
